faqs.answer: For cooking, usually yes, the difference is small. For baking, use measuring spoons. Leavening and salt need the exact amount, and a drawer spoon is not a measuring spoon.

howToSteps.name: Read the tablespoons
howToSteps.text: Find the amount in tablespoons in your recipe. Halves and whole numbers are the usual amounts.

howToSteps.name: Multiply by 3
howToSteps.text: Tablespoons times 3 gives teaspoons. One tablespoon is 3 teaspoons, two is 6, four is 12.

howToSteps.name: Use measuring spoons
howToSteps.text: A measuring tablespoon is exactly 3 measuring teaspoons. Cutlery spoons from the drawer are close but not exact, so use the measuring set for baking.

howToSteps.name: Level dry spoons
howToSteps.text: Fill the spoon, then sweep a knife across the top. A heaped teaspoon holds far more than a level one.

name: Tablespoons to Teaspoons
title: Tablespoons to Teaspoons Converter
tutorial: Three teaspoons make a tablespoon. It is the smallest conversion in the kitchen and the one you use most, because spices, baking powder, vanilla, and salt all live at this scale. One tablespoon of paprika is 3 teaspoons. Half a tablespoon is 1 1/2 teaspoons.

The reason the conversion matters is precision. A teaspoon of baking soda too much can turn a cake bitter and soapy, and a teaspoon too little leaves it flat. Recipes that say one tablespoon of baking powder mean exactly 3 teaspoons, not a heaped spoonful and a guess.

Halving and doubling recipes runs through this conversion constantly. Half a tablespoon is 1 1/2 teaspoons. Double a tablespoon is 6 teaspoons, which is 2 tablespoons. When a recipe scales down to a single serving, the tablespoon amounts shrink into teaspoons, and this is the page that does the maths.

Spoons are not all the same, and the set in your drawer is what the recipe means. A measuring tablespoon is 3 measuring teaspoons, exactly. A soup spoon from the cutlery drawer is not a measuring tablespoon, and a teaspoon from the drawer is not a measuring teaspoon. They are close, but close is not exact, and baking notices.
For liquids, fill the spoon to the brim. For dry spices, fill it and level it with a knife. A heaped teaspoon of cayenne is twice a level one, and that is the difference between warm and inedible.
